title: Tool design and token cost
summary: Every tool definition and every tool result costs tokens and shapes the model's choices. Good tools have few, well-named, task-shaped operations, unambiguous parameters and bounded, meaningful results.
useIf: You are writing or reviewing tools, or an agent picks the wrong tool, runs slowly or costs too much per turn.
avoidIf: You expose one tool per API endpoint because the API already looks that way.

explain.md: A host places tool definitions (name, description, schema, annotations) in the model's context on every request, so cost scales with how many tools you expose and how long each definition is. MCP's client guidance illustrates about 150,000 tokens of definitions up front versus about 2,000 with on-demand loading, and says to switch strategies once definitions pass a threshold such as 1% to 5% of the context window. It is an illustration, not a benchmark [[r8]]. Anthropic estimates that a typical five-server setup can use about 55k tokens of definitions [[r19]].

explain.example: 45 tools x 500 tokens = 22,500 tokens, which is about 17.6 percent of a 128,000-token context before the user says anything.

explain.md: The spec adds mechanics: names SHOULD be 1 to 128 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore, hyphen and dot, and an aggregator SHOULD prefix names with a server identifier because the server `name` is not guaranteed unique. Do not mark sensitive parameters with `x-mcp-header`, since header values are visible to network intermediaries [[r6]]. Design advice and numbers in the table come from Anthropic's tool-writing guide [[r14]].

explain.title: Prefix style matters
explain.md: Anthropic found that prefix versus suffix namespacing has non-trivial effects on tool-use evaluations and that effects vary by model, so choose by running your own evaluation.

pitfalls.symptom: The agent picks the wrong tool among near-duplicates
pitfalls.fix: Merge them or state in each description when to use it and when not to, then re-evaluate

pitfalls.symptom: Token spend per turn doubled after a new server was added
pitfalls.cause: All definitions are injected on every request
pitfalls.fix: Measure definition tokens, prune, and apply tool search past your threshold

pitfalls.symptom: Runs fail when a tool returns a huge list
pitfalls.cause: No pagination, filter or truncation defaults
pitfalls.fix: Add limits with sensible defaults and steer the model to narrower queries

scenarios.title: Wrapping a 60-endpoint REST API
scenarios.situation: A team wants to expose its REST API to agents. It has 60 endpoints, most used in a few repeating workflows. Latency and cost matter.
unknowns: Which workflows do agents actually run?
Do other consumers need raw endpoints?
scenarios.question: How should you design the tools?

options.name: Around 8 workflow tools named by task and namespaced, built from observed transcripts
options.why: Fewer definitions, fewer round trips and clearer choices for the model.
options.tradeoff: More server logic, and rarely used endpoints need another route.

options.name: All 60 endpoints behind tool search
options.tradeoff: An extra search step and added cache and accuracy concerns.

options.name: One tool per endpoint with generic names
options.why: Large token cost and ambiguous choices.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable for a tiny API or a quick prototype.

flips.then: Expose the raw tools with tool search until usage data appears.

scenarios.takeaway: Design for the agent's tasks, not for the API's shape.

scenarios.title: Two servers both expose `search`
scenarios.situation: A host aggregates a wiki server and a ticket server. Both define a tool called `search`. The model sometimes queries the wrong system.
unknowns: Does the host prefix names itself?
scenarios.question: How do you remove the ambiguity?

options.name: Prefix names with a server identifier and write descriptions that say when to use each
options.why: The spec advises prefixing for collisions and clear descriptions guide selection.
options.tradeoff: Slightly longer names and a prefix convention to maintain.

options.name: Ask one team to rename its tool
options.why: Fixes the collision at the source.
options.tradeoff: Cross-team coordination and the next collision remains possible.

options.name: Disambiguate using the server's self-reported `name`
options.why: The server `name` is not guaranteed unique and SHOULD NOT be relied on for disambiguation.
options.tradeoff: Use only identifiers your host assigns and controls.

flips.then: Rename at the source with a namespaced convention.

flips.if: The host already prefixes names with a server identifier it assigns
flips.then: The collision is handled, and you need only clearer descriptions.

scenarios.takeaway: Namespaces come from the integrator, not from self-reported names.

quiz.q: A host exposes 45 tools averaging 500 tokens each. The model's context window is 128,000 tokens. What percentage of the context do the definitions use?
quiz.explain: 45 x 500 = 22,500 tokens. 22,500 / 128,000 is about 17.6 percent, far above the 1 to 5 percent threshold the MCP client guidance suggests for switching to progressive discovery.

quiz.q: An agent often calls `list_events` and then `create_event` with a guessed user. Which redesign best matches the guidance?
options: Add more tools for each field
A `schedule_event` tool that finds availability and creates the event, with a `user_id` parameter
quiz.explain: Consolidating chained operations into a task-shaped tool and naming parameters unambiguously reduces calls and guesses. More tools raise cost, removing descriptions hurts selection and larger results cost tokens.

flashcards.front: What is the definition cost of a tool catalog?
flashcards.back: Tool count times average tokens per definition, paid on every request. Measure it and compare with your context window.

flashcards.front: Name three tool design rules from Anthropic's guide.
flashcards.back: Consolidate chained operations, namespace names, and return bounded, meaningful results. Also name parameters unambiguously and evaluate with realistic tasks.

flashcards.front: Why prefix tool names when aggregating servers?
flashcards.back: Names are unique per server only, and the server `name` is not guaranteed unique, so the integrator should prefix with an identifier it controls.
